item.title: Get to know LSU basketball center Michael Ruzic
item.description: After a complete offseason rebuild, LSU basketball has its roster for the 2026-27 season. Coach Will Wade and his staff took an abnormal route to find a new group of players to rep purple and gold. Most of the roster is comprised of international players and fifth-year seniors exhausting their college eligibility. While there is a lot of basketball experience, there’s a new face in every corner of the Tigers’ locker room. With so many new faces, having a spark coming off the bench or serving as a key sixth man is key for a team developing chemistry. The Tigers have just that in 7-foot center Michael Ruzic, who brings more overseas experience to their roster. Here are three things to know about the Tigers' freshman Croatian center. A potential NBA Draft pick When Ruzic was 16 years old, the buzz had started surrounding his potential of making it to the NBA. At the 2023 Adidas EuroCamp, he was widely regarded at one of the premier showcases for international prospects in Europe. The Adidas EuroCamp has become a breeding ground for discoving overseas talent, including Victor Wembanyama and Nikola Jokic. Ruzic averaged 12 points and four rebounds over three games at the Adidas EuroCamp while shooting 73% from the field and an impressive 71% from deep. Since then, Ruzic has continued to grow into his 7-foot and 240-pound frame. Now 20, Ruzic has legitimate positional size and is key example of a potential rotational big man in the NBA. Ruzic comes from an Olympian family There was no question that Ruzic would be an athlete. Outside of his tall stature and long wingspan, he comes from a line of Olympians but not in the sport many would guess. Ruzic’s mother, Barbara, is considered one of the best Croatian volleyball players of all time. His grandfather, Ivica Jelic, was also a volleyball player, competing in the 1980 Summer Olympics. His aunt, Vesna Jelic, also competed at the 2000 Summer Olympics. item.title: Dan Campbell Makes Bold Declaration Ahead of Patriots Matchup Goes Viral
item.description: Dan Campbell does not expect the Detroit Lions to feel like strangers in Munich. With Amon-Ra St. Brown helping connect the franchise to German fans, Detroit’s head coach believes Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots could sound familiar. Speaking Friday during his first press conference in Germany, Campbell reiterated a bold declaration he said he made back in the spring. Now that the Lions have arrived, he is looking forward to seeing that connection turn into support inside the stadium. The Lions will face the Patriots at Munich’s Allianz Arena on Sunday . Campbell’s message to the people welcoming his team was straightforward: Detroit appreciates the reception, and it wants to give those fans a performance worth celebrating. Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell on the field before the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. He credited that connection with helping Detroit feel at home thousands of miles from Michigan. “We feel like this is going to be a home game,” Campbell said during his Munich press conference . “I said this way back in the spring. It’s like, ‘Hey, we’re Germany’s team.’ “St. Brown, we’re going to hang on to his coattails, and we’re excited to be here.” St. Brown’s influence has already been evident in the lighter moments of the trip, including helping Campbell navigate an attempted German motivational message . But Campbell’s expectation of a supportive crowd also reflects what he has watched Lions fans do on the road back home. item.title: Nikita Johnson Won the Indy NXT Title With Zero Poles, Two Wins and 656 of 656 Laps. Coyne Noticed
item.description: Nikita Johnson at Barber Motorsports Park, where he made his first INDYCAR test with Dale Coyne Racing. Photo: James Black Nikita Johnson spent 2026 building the quietest championship résumé Indy NXT has produced: two wins, no poles, all 656 laps completed, and a top-10 finish in every one of the 17 races. On Nov. 10, Dale Coyne Racing announced he will carry that record into the 2027 NTT IndyCar Series in one of the team’s Honda-powered entries. Youngest champion in series history, racing at home in St. Pete. That’s the headline. What Coyne actually bought is a finisher, not a qualifier, and for a team that ended 19th and 22nd in the points, that’s exactly what it needs. The zero in the pole column is also the number to watch. A title built on not losing points The facts are on the record. Johnson clinched at 18 years, 3 months and 12 days old, the youngest champion in the series’ history, and the series’ driver page credits him with 585 points, 51 laps led and no poles for Cape Motorsports Powered by ECR. IndyCar’s own feature adds eight podiums and ten top fives. He beat Enzo Fittipaldi by 29 points. That is a championship won by the bottom of the results sheet as much as the top. Never worse than tenth in 17 starts, and no lap lost to a mistake, is a different skill from setting a one-lap benchmark. It is also a skill rookies in IndyCar are rarely credited with, because the cars punish the ones who overreach. What Coyne is actually shopping for Look at what Coyne is replacing. Its two 2026 cars finished 19th (Romain Grosjean, 259 points) and 22nd (Dennis Hauger, 228) in the final standings . Hauger is leaving for AJ Foyt Racing, a move that is part of the Foyt rookie-development math we broke down earlier this fall. Coyne, by its own team history, has focused on developing emerging drivers since 1990. That is analysis, not a quote from anyone at the team: a back-half program does not need a rookie who gambles on the opening lap. It needs one who brings the car home, so engineers get clean data across a full race distance. Speed without finishing can look like Louis Foster leading 32 laps and still finishing 22nd at Markham. Johnson’s season is the reverse: little glory in qualifying, almost no waste on Sundays. Johnson’s 2026 INDY NXT season was celebrated at the series’ Victory Lap Banquet. Photo: Chris Owens The test told you the real homework Johnson’s first IndyCar test came Oct. 26 at Barber Motorsports Park, in a Coyne car shared with Formula 2 driver Alex Dunne. Dunne took the morning, Johnson the afternoon. His summary afterward was blunt: “It was faster, more downforce. It was surreal.” The adjustment he flagged was braking. IndyCar runs carbon brakes; his junior cars used steel. Braking is the right thing to be learning, because it is where a patient driver can lose time without losing the car. item.title: Tuchel does not expect White to give up on England career
item.description: Tuchel does not expect White to give up on England career England supporters continued to boo Ben White during the recent match against Croatia, but Thomas Tuchel does not believe the reaction will stop the Arsenal defender from accepting future international call-ups. The hostility towards White stems from his decision to leave England’s camp during the 2022 World Cup following a reported disagreement with members of the coaching staff. He subsequently stayed away from the national team until that management group departed and Tuchel took charge. Since becoming England manager, the German has selected White whenever the defender has been fit enough to represent his country. Tuchel believes the Arsenal player deserves his place in the squad and remains an important option despite the competition for places at right back. England have considerable depth in that position, but White remains one of the country’s strongest options. Tuchel has also seen no indication that the defender has lost his enthusiasm for representing his country. The England manager believes White remains committed to the national team and expects him to continue accepting invitations despite the negative reaction from some supporters. Tuchel dismisses concerns over White’s future Asked whether the booing could make White reconsider his international career, Tuchel played down the possibility and insisted the defender had shown the right attitude since he became manager. Speaking via ESPN , the German explained that White has consistently demonstrated his commitment whenever he has joined the England squad. He said: “I don’t think so. I don’t want to make it bigger than it is. I don’t think so. I don’t hope so. He seems to be always committed and always dedicated and excited to come to camp and get the call-up. “He had too many injuries. No, I don’t hope so. He is a high-quality player and I honestly don’t even know what happened and what were the deep reasons and the situation that he left camp. “Since I am in charge, there is no reason to doubt his commitment, his passion. I don’t want to think in these extreme terms at the moment.” (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) White remains an option for England Tuchel’s comments suggest he has no intention of allowing the reaction from supporters to influence his decision to select White. The defender has continued to receive opportunities whenever available, and the manager clearly values what he brings to the team. item.title: Red Wings Prospect Pool in Elite Company
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While Steve Yzerman is no longer the general manager and President of Hockey operations for the Detroit Red Wings, the former Stanley Cup winning captain of the team. However, the now former GM left the team a parting gift after his seven years in the GM chair, with the league’s 7th ranked prospect pool according to Elite Prospects ‘ latest guide, released in partnership with the NHL. The next-gen nucleus Detroit has five players in the top 100 of the outlet’s rankings, topped by goaltender Trey Augustine at no. 8. The former Michigan State Spartan standout and 2026 Mike Richter Award winner began his first professional season with the Grand Rapids Griffins this year. After a somewhat rocky start to his career in the AHL , Augustine is 4-1-2 through his first eight games and has a 2.56 GAA and .909 sv %. It helps that the Red Wings other prospect ranked inside the top 20, Carter Bear , is tied for the AHL lead with 18 points in just 13 games played. At the NHL level, Michael Brandsegg-Nygard is having a hard-hitting rookie season and has 10 points in 20 games. The Norwegian winger slots in as the outlet’s 25th ranked prospect across all 32 teams. Red Wings college prospects Max Plante (no. 55) and JP Hurlbert (no. 92) round out the team’s prospects inside the top 100. Both have been having quieter years, although in Plante’s case he has been sidelined by injury for the past month. Meanwhile, Detroit’s 2026 first round draft pick, Hurlbert, has two goals and two assists through nine games with the University of Michigan Wolverines. Detroit traded the no. 26 ranked prospect on the list, goaltender Sebastian Cossa , to the Utah Mammoth to select Hurlbert in this past year’s draft. The Red Wings’ prospect pool has plenty of players who project to the NHL level but overall seems to lack a game-breaking or top end talent, especially at center. With a grain of salt While the Red Wings prospect pool ranks 7th across the league according to the outlet, for the vast majority of names on the list, they still have to prove they can actually play in the NHL. Some, like Brandsegg-Nygård and no. 1 overall ranked prospect Gavin McKenna are already in the middle of their rookie seasons in the Show. Others, like Hurlbert, are years away from even sniffing the ice in a professional game. It won’t be for another couple of years until Red Wings fans know if this crop of prospects will actually be making significant contributions for the team. Obviously some, like Bear and Michal Postava , are closer to playing at Little Caesars Arena than others, and there seems to be a little more certainty in what they will look like playing in a Red Wings uniform, but until their skates actually hit the ice and they get a full season or two under their belt, no one knows what they have with most of these players. item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown questionable for Lions' Germany game vs Patriots
item.description: MUNICH − Amon-Ra St. Brown is listed as questionable for the Detroit Lions ' game against the New England Patriots in Germany, but the Lions wide receiver said he's "excited" to play football in the country where his mother was born . “I just want to say thank you to everyone that’s here. All the fans, I can’t wait for the game," St. Brown said Friday, Nov. 13. "I’m so excited to be playing football in Germany with my teammates. It’s really honestly a dream come true. I haven’t even played the game yet and it feels amazing. The love, the support, the energy. I can’t wait to see the fans so, yeah, I’m ready." St. Brown was listed as questionable on the Lions' injury report with a rib injury that has nagged him since last week. He was listed as a limited participant in the Lions' walk-through Friday at FC Bayern Campus. Last week, St. Brown played through his injury and led the Lions with eight catches and 86 yards receiving in a 19-9 win at Miami. Running back Sione Vaki also was listed as questionable, though he was upgraded to a limited participant from a non-participant in practice. TRENDING: Germany game is a return to football roots for Amon-Ra St. Brown Previously, the Lions ruled out cornerback D.J. Reed, center Cade Mays and safety Kerby Joseph . Reed, Mays and Joseph did not travel with the Lions (6-2) to Germany, and Joseph remains on the physically unable to perform list. Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. item.description: Terrance McKinney badly missed weight for UFC 334 | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC Terrance McKinney is lucky to still be fighting at UFC 334. Saturday’s event is headlined by a pair of title fights featuring Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit, and Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes, but McKinney caused a stir at Friday’s official weigh-ins for the wrong reasons. The all-action lightweight registered at 160.2 pounds on the scale, more than four pounds over the limit for his preliminary bout with Jim Miller (155.6). Fortunately for McKinney, Miller has agreed to proceed with the bout at a catchweight with McKinney forfeiting 30 percent of his purse. McKinney was quick to release a statement to social media apologizing to Miller and declaring that he will soon move up to the 170-pound division. See McKinney’s comments and watch his weigh-in below. View this post on Instagram “I want to apologize to everyone and UFC for missing weight,” McKinney wrote. “I’ve never missed weight in my life and I’m sorry, but ship has sailed for 155. It’s official, my last bout at lightweight. I’m trusting in God will make sure I’m ready for whatever comes at welterweight.” “I want to thank Jim Miller personally for still taking the fight. He’s a real gangster and also want to apologize to him for failing to make. Jim f*cking Miller GOATed, appreciate you for letting dream still be a reality fighting at MSG.” One other preliminary fighter, Juan Diaz, also missed weight, coming in 0.4 pounds over the 135-pound limit (including one-pound allowance for a non-title fight). His bout with Alatengheili proceeds as a catchweight with Diaz forfeiting 20 percent of his purse as penalty. Gane and Hokit both took their time arriving at Friday’s weigh-ins, but had no issues making weight for the heavyweight title main event, coming in well under the 265-pounds limit with Gane at 242.6 and Hokit at 231.4. The first two fighters to weigh in were Harrison and Nunes, who both hit championship weight at 135 pounds on the dot. item.title: How have rookie QBs fared historically vs. Sean McVay and the Rams?
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams won’t be facing Jacoby Brissett on Sunday like they did in Week 6. They won’t be facing his backup, Gardner Minshew, either. With Brissett traded and Minshew on injured reserve, the Arizona Cardinals are turning to third-round rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. They probably didn’t plan to start Beck this season, but Brissett’s struggles and Minshew’s injury have forced their hand. On Sunday, Beck will attempt to do something only two other quarterbacks have done against the Rams since 2017: beat Sean McVay. Historically, rookie quarterbacks have struggled against the Rams. The odds are against Beck to buck that trend; Arizona is a 9.5-point underdog in this game, making the Rams heavy favorites despite being on the road. Rookie QB stats vs. Rams since 2017 With McVay as the head coach, the Rams are 9-2 against rookie quarterbacks. The only two rookies to beat the Rams were Caleb Williams in 2024 and Tua Tagovailoa in 2020. Tagovailoa only threw for 93 yards and one touchdown in that shocking win against Jared Goff and the Rams, while Williams had just 157 yards and a score in the Bears ' 24-18 win over Los Angeles in 2024. In total, rookie quarterbacks have 14 touchdown passes and only five interceptions against the Rams, and all 11 of them have taken at least one sack. The Rams sacked Cam Ward and Davis Mills five times in those respective games, and Kyler Murray six times in 2019. Of the Rams' nine wins against rookie quarterbacks, six have been by at least 14 points, with the other three victories all being by six or seven points. Beck is in an even tougher spot with this being his first NFL start, especially considering he only played one preseason game this summer. But he was a winner in college at both Georgia and Miami, and as a third-round pick, the Cardinals clearly think highly of him. Kickoff is set for 4:05 p.m. ET on Sunday afternoon. item.title: San Antonio-area football powerhouse celebrates 100th win for head coach
item.description: Steele head coach David Saenz earned his 100th career victory with a 44-24 win over Reagan in the Class 6A, Division I bi-district round. (Courtesy of Byron P Steele II High School) As high school football playoffs officially began on Thursday night, November 12, one of the San Antonio-area's top football programs celebrated a major milestone for its longtime head coach. Steele ended Thursday night with a 44-24 victory over Reagan in the bi-district round of the Class 6A, Division I playoffs. The Knights have now gone seven straight seasons with at least one playoff win, and Thursday's victory was the 100th career win for head coach David Saenz. "The Knights are moving on to Round 2 and Head Coach, David Saenz, earned his 100th career win as a head coach," Byron P. Steele II High School wrote in a Facebook post. "Congrats to the athletes, coaches, and entire Steele community on the victory!" Saenz was promoted to head coach in 2017 after Scott Lehnhoff was promoted to Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City ISD athletic director. Prior to that, he'd worked as an assistant coach with the Knights for 10 years, helping them to their first state title in 2010 and runner-up finishes in 2011 and 2016. As head coach, Saenz's teams have averaged 10 wins per season and have won at least 11 games since 2021. His best finish as Knights head coach came in 2023 when Steele made it to the state semifinals before falling to Humble Summer Creek. Along the way Saenz has coached NFL players such as JT Woods (Los Angeles Chargers), Caden Sterns (Denver Broncos) and Jaylon Jones (Indianapolis Colts). Saenz's former athletes currently playing college football include Jonathan Hatton Jr. (Oklahoma), Julian Hugo (Arizona State), Jalen Cooper (SMU) and Dontae Carter (Vanderbilt). Steele will now play the winner of Lake Travis vs. Buda Johnson in the area round at a date and time to be determined. item.description: Carsten Cramer and Armin Papperger on Dortmund's Rheinmetall partnership The official sponsorship agreement between Borussia Dortmund and Rheinmetall expires on 30 June 2027 and will not be renewed. Carsten Cramer, Chairman of BVB’s Management Board, and Armin Papperger, CEO of Rheinmetall, discuss the reasons behind the decision, their collaboration over the past few years and how they will continue working together. Mr Cramer, the official sponsorship agreement with Rheinmetall, which has been in place since summer 2024, will not be renewed beyond 30 June 2027. How did this decision come about? Carsten Cramer: “First of all, I want to stress that we did not make this decision alone, but jointly with Rheinmetall. We are of course aware that our partnership has been the subject of controversy from the outset. We are familiar with the criticism from our members and some of our fans. At the 2024 General Meeting, members voted on a motion not to extend the partnership agreement with Rheinmetall beyond 2027. Naturally, we took this into account in our discussions with Rheinmetall and treated it seriously.” Mr Papperger, how did you find the discussions with BVB on this issue? Armin Papperger: “The discussions were very open, constructive and built on trust, just as our entire partnership has been from the very beginning. Carsten Cramer and I spoke very openly about the concerns of BVB and its members. We were equally open in sharing our own thoughts. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.description: Latest Man City update reveals when they will face Premier League punishments Manchester City Face Premier League Sanctions as £900m Financial Case Reaches Crucial Stage Manchester City’s long-running financial controversy is approaching another defining moment, with the Premier League champions facing the prospect of significant sanctions in 2027 if their forthcoming appeal proves unsuccessful. According to a report by the Financial Times, City’s appeal against findings that they breached Premier League financial regulations is scheduled for mid-December. A decision is expected early next year, potentially setting the stage for punishments that could fundamentally alter the club’s immediate future. For English football, the implications extend considerably beyond the Etihad Stadium. Photo: IMAGO Manchester City Appeal Could Decide Premier League Future The independent commission’s September ruling represented a remarkable development in one of football’s most consequential legal disputes. City were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges originally brought against them in 2023, with the investigation examining financial arrangements spanning nine years. Central to those findings was the allegation that Manchester City artificially inflated their financial position by more than £900million. The commission concluded that certain sponsorship arrangements involved additional funding from a private Abu Dhabi investment company ultimately controlled by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, City’s owner. City’s appeal now represents a critical opportunity to challenge those conclusions. Potential punishments include substantial financial penalties, points deductions and, in the most extreme circumstances, expulsion from the competition. A significant points deduction could reshape a title race, influence European qualification or fundamentally change the competitive landscape. Expulsion would raise even more complicated questions concerning league membership and future participation. Further appeals against any punishment could extend proceedings beyond the conclusion of the current season in May. The 25-year-old has quickly become one of the more closely watched wide players in the Premier League after an excellent start to life on the south coast. item.title: Chuba Hubbard And Panthers Tight Ends Form Perfect Chemistry
item.description: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Chuba Hubbard and the Carolina Panthers ‘ tight ends have found a rare rhythm that few teams possess this season. In return, the tight ends are seeing their best production in years because Hubbard commands so much defensive attention. Hubbard has already matched his entire touch count from last season with 134 carries through eight games. He has also surpassed his rushing total from that year, reaching 619 yards and five touchdowns. The tight end room is feeding off this momentum, with players like Mitchell Evans calling the relationship a “push-pull kind of thing, yin-yang.” Evans noted that the group is blocking “pretty d—- well,” which helps Hubbard gain yards. When Hubbard runs well, defenses respect the run game, which opens up passing lanes for the tight ends. A Shared Standard of Excellence The connection goes beyond simple play calls. Head coach Dave Canales sees Hubbard as the standard-bearer for what the organization wants to be. “What I love about Chuba is that the things that we talk about wanting to be as an organization, he represents those in spades,” Canales said. The coach praised Hubbard’s preparation and work ethic, noting that he sometimes has to “reel him in and call him back a little bit because he goes so hard.” This intensity sets the tone for the entire room, including the tight ends who block for him every play. Tight end Tommy Tremble emphasized that Hubbard’s elite level of play forces opponents to respect the run. “If he wasn’t playing as good as he has been, people wouldn’t respect our run game,” Tremble said. He explained that when the defense respects the run, it opens up the pass game for him, Darren Waller, and the rest of the tight end room. The running back is doing the heavy lifting, and the tight ends are capitalizing on the space he creates. Preparing for a Tough Test The Panthers face a critical test this Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. The Saints rank 29th in the league against the run, a weakness Hubbard is poised to exploit. Both teams enter the matchup with 3-5 records, making this game vital for the division lead. Hubbard has practiced fully after taking a rest day on Wednesday, while backup Jonathon Brooks is also trending toward a full return despite a groin issue. Hubbard carries 70.8% of the team’s rushing attempts, showing the coaching staff trusts him to handle the load.
